newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hagemeyer sees 1997 foods margin improving.
newsitem.headline: Hagemeyer sees 1997 foods margin improving.

text.p: Dutch trading company Hagemeyer NV said on Thursday the operating profit margin in its U.S. speciality foods trading business will improve substantially in 1997.
In 1996 the operating profit as a percentage of sales dropped to 1.8 percent from 4.4 percent in 1995.
"We expect to show a substantial improvement this year," Hagemeyer chairman Andrew Land told Reuters.
"Our aim is to improve the margin (in speciality foods) to 4.5 percent and we will reach this in the next 12 to 18 months," Land said.
He said that he did not expect to make up the whole 1996 dip in the current year. "But we are heading for it," he added.
Sales in the speciality foods sector rose to just over 722 million guilders in 1996 from almost 620 million in 1995.
"Our priority is to improve the margin, but we also do not exclude a takeover in our speciality foods business in the United States this year," Land said.
Hagemeyer wants to expand its business in speciality foods to over one billion guilders within a few years.
Hagemeyer's trading business also includes consumer and professional products, which had 1996 turnover of 3.82 billion guilders and a operating profit margin of 6.3 percent.

Electrical distribution yielded 1996 sales of 2.91 billion guilders and a margin of 5.7 percent and automotive and technical products had a turnover of 762 million guilders and a margin of 6.4 percent in the same year.
Land said the company was holding on to its aim to show an overall profit margin (operating profit as percentage to sales) of over five percent.
Hong Kong's First Pacific Co owns an economic stake of approximately 36 percent in Hagemeyer.
